speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have been experiencing episodes of dizziness and vertigo; could you describe exactly what those sensations feel like and how long each episode lasts? Additionally, have you noticed any accompanying symptoms like hearing loss, ringing in your ears, or nausea?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. The fact that your dizziness is position-dependent and feels like spinning is very telling. To narrow this down, does the spinning sensation start and stop very quickly (usually lasting less than a minute) when you change your head position? Also, have you noticed any new hearing loss or tinnitus in the affected ear?

REQUEST TEST: Audiometry
REQUEST IMAGES: Dix-Hallpike

Positional Testing: Dix-Hallpike Manoeuvre: Positive for right-sided horizontal nystagmus when moving from sitting to supine position, suggestive of BPPV.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV) of the right posterior canal.

Given the positive Dix-Hallpike test showing right-sided nystagmus and the exclusion of Meniere's via audiometry, I will proceed with a canalith repositioning maneuver (Epley maneuver) to treat the condition. Do you have any history of neck problems or recent ear surgery that might contraindicate this procedure?
